=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): alternate (leaves are attached at different nodes along the stem in a spiral pattern)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (leaves are grouped densely at the tips of the branches)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3.	Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (leaves consist of a single blade without distinct leaflets)
    4.	Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A
    5.	Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A
    6.	Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A
C. Leaf Morphology
    7.	Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.): entire (leaf margins appear smooth and continuous without teeth)
    8.	Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): lanceolate (leaves are elongated and taper towards both the base and the apex)
    9.	Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acuminate (the tip tapers to a slender point)
    10.	Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): cuneate (the leaf narrows gradually to a wedge-shaped base)
    11.	Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (a single midrib runs from base to apex with lateral veins branching off)
    12.	Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): visible and distinct (lateral veins branch off the midrib at an angle and curve towards the margin)
    13.	Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): shiny (the upper leaf surface reflects light, indicating a glossy texture)
    14.	Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs on the leaf surface)
    15.	Petiole length (short / long): short (the stalk connecting the leaf to the stem is very brief)
    16.	Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (the petiole appears round in cross-section)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17.	Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): woody (the stem appears lignified and rigid)
    18.	Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (the stem surface appears smooth without visible hairs)
    19.	Stem color: brown (the visible parts of the stem are brown)
    20.	Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (the stem lacks obvious ridges or large lenticels)
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21.	Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipules are clearly visible at the leaf bases)
    22.	Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed
    23.	Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent
    24.	Tendrils (present / absent): absent
F. Notes: A pink plastic tag is tied around the stem. Some leaves exhibit minor physical damage such as small holes.
